description:
The DEGENERATE FORM of CBTRN01C's post-end-of-file lookup, and the case that proves the quirk is structural rather than incidental: an empty daily transaction file, over which the lookup STILL RUNS. The daily file is seeded as a dataset that EXISTS and holds no row - "empty": true with its declared 350-byte width and its CVTRA06Y copybook - which is a different assertion from not seeding it at all, and only this shape reaches the first-read end-of-file branch. So 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT at app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:203-225 reports '10' on its very first READ, the nested ladder at :204-212 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT at :208, 16 matches the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at :144, and :217 moves 'Y' into END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE. No record is ever displayed, because the inner guard at :167 opens after that READ and closes at :169 and covers ONLY the DISPLAY at :168. THE THREE STATEMENTS AT :170-172 AND THE ACCOUNT READ AT :173-179 SIT OUTSIDE THAT GUARD AND RUN ANYWAY. This is deliberate and is the whole subject of the case: the trailing lookup is not a defect to be corrected, suppressed or annotated away, and hoisting :170-172 inside the guard - or skipping the iteration whose read hit end of file - makes this case fail, which is exactly the point (practice B5). The card number :171 moves into XREF-CARD-NUM is whatever the DALYTRAN-RECORD area holds, and on this path nothing has ever been moved into it: a READ ... INTO does not disturb its receiving area AT END, and here there was no successful read before it either, so the area still holds the declared value of a PIC X(16) item - SIXTEEN SPACES. No cross-reference row carries a card number of sixteen spaces, so the keyed read at :229-230 takes the INVALID KEY phrase, :232 displays 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOR XREF' and :233 moves 4 into WS-XREF-READ-STATUS, which fails the test at :173 and so 3000-READ-ACCOUNT is never reached on this run. Control falls to the ELSE at :180 and the single four-operand DISPLAY at :181-183 emits one 92-character line whose card number and transaction id are BOTH blank - 'CARD NUMBER ' + sixteen spaces + ' COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-' + sixteen spaces - because DALYTRAN-ID is untouched for the same reason DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM is. Four lines in total therefore: the :156 banner, those two, and the :195 banner. A run performs recordsRead + 1 lookups ALWAYS, and this case pins the boundary at recordsRead = 0, where the identity still holds and one lookup happens over no records at all. case01 pins the same repeat after one clean record and case06 pins that the repeat uses the LAST record's card rather than the first; this case pins that it happens even when there is no record. expectedReturnCode is 0: CBTRN01C contains no MOVE statement targeting RETURN-CODE anywhere, and APPL-RESULT reaching 16 only terminates the PERFORM UNTIL at :164 - it never becomes a process return code - so an empty input is a normal completion and the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is unreached. expectedWrites is EMPTY as a POSITIVE assertion rather than an absence of interest: a scan of the source finds zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements, all six files are OPEN INPUT, and the six WRITES-channel dataset expectations below say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width - including CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE, which :158-160 open and :189-191 close but which no READ in this program ever touches, and which are therefore absent from "inputs" because a dataset the case says nothing about is omitted rather than declared empty. expectedFinalState carries no row expectation because the only dataset this run could have changed holds nothing to pin; DALYTRAN is instead pinned on the FINAL_STATE channel at a row count of zero and its declared 350-byte width, which asserts that an empty input file is still an empty input file afterwards. The cross-reference row is seeded at the 36 bytes cardxref.txt actually holds and is NOT pre-padded; the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14) once, at seed time (gate G16, risk R-F). The account row is acctdata.txt row 7 at its full 300 bytes, whose CVACT01Y FILLER X(178) is space-filled across bytes 123-300 and whose ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the copybook's own misspelling (requirement I1); neither the cross-reference row nor the account row is read on this path, and both are seeded so that the run's silence is attributable to the empty daily file and to nothing else. R1 and practice B4 caveat, documented and not 'fixed' on either side: the mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source header 'Post the records from daily transaction file' both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing at all; CBTRN01C is also the migration's orphan, invoked by no EXEC PGM= in app/jcl or app/proc, so jobParameters is empty because there is no PARM for one to come from and the job carries no trigger (gate G13, requirement I4). A second divergence is recorded here for the same reason rather than absorbed silently: the build prompt for this fixture described case04 as a two-record run pinning that the stale card is the SECOND record's, while CBTRN01CParityTest - authored against this same ParityCase constructor - allocates that assertion to case06 and allocates the empty-input degenerate form to case04. The test class is followed, because it is the compiled contract the gate executes and because it states that a shipped fixture set must return the same twenty ParityCase values it builds; taking case04 for the two-record variant would have duplicated case06 and left the degenerate form - the only case that pins the recordsRead + 1 identity at its zero boundary - unasserted. Baseline provenance, practice B12: these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl read paragraph by paragraph, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300, every offset mechanically diffable by eye - practice B11) and against the real ASCII fixtures, from which both seeded rows are read verbatim rather than retyped. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services, so CALL 'CEE3ABD' cannot be reached at all. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default, and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock, so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practices B7 and B8). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", so no user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G30 (the :204-212 status ladder judged in source order, '10' on the first read), G47 (the '00' opens, the '10' first read that is a normal boundary rather than an error, and the INVALID KEY arm of the keyed cross-reference read) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path). G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.

THE READ SEQUENCE, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every read this run must issue, in order and with the key it is given, and it says three things no byte fingerprint can. First, WHICH VERB: the daily file's read is readNext because :203 reads sequentially and takes whatever record is next, while the cross reference and the account are read at :229 and :243 by a key the program built - a translation that turned either keyed read into a browse would produce identical SYSOUT. Second, HOW MANY: there is always one readNext more than there are records, because the loop at :164-186 reads again to learn it is at end of file, and the lookup that follows sits at :170-172 OUTSIDE the guard that closed at :169 - so the last lookup runs on the card number the previous record left in WORKING-STORAGE. Third, WITH WHAT: the key is recorded as declared, so on the trailing lookup it is the PREVIOUS record's card number, and on a run whose daily file was empty it is absent entirely because the record area never held anything. Every entry here was derived from this case's own expected DISPLAY lines - one echo per record at :168, one lookup block per iteration - and never from a run.
